incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: deploy-canary-high-error-rate (sev2) for service=redwood-inference-gateway, canary group=canary-a. Started 2026-03-15T14:22:25Z (ts: 2470012345)

Emma H: I'm seeing a 5xx spike in the canary telemetry dashboard - error rate jumped from 0.3% -> 9% over last 5m. Latency also up ~200ms p50. Can we drain traffic from canary-A now?

Raj P: Agree, reduce canary weight. Traffic-router currently at weight=15% for canary-A. I'll attempt a drain, but I saw a previous issue where the feature-flag toggle timed out due to k/v lock. Heads up.

OpsBot: drain request accepted: "traffic-router set-weight canary-a 0" -> job queued (job-id: tr-9832). Progress: 0/3 shards updated.

Santiago: Quick customer impact note: two Enterprise customers (acme-corp, finlytics) hit the 502s during their batch inference windows. Estimated 1.1% of overall requests (spike window). We're currently in canary->prod gradual ramp; most prod traffic unaffected.

Avani: Trying feature flag flip now: `curl -X POST https://flags.red/api/v1/toggle -d '{"flag":"canary-a-enabled","value":false}'` -> 504 from flags service. Looks like flags API is overloaded.

Emma H: If flags are flapping, let's not rely on that. Manual traffic-router drain + verify is safer.

Raj P: OpsBot shows drain jobs stuck on shard-2 with "pending db-connections: 12". Looks like some long-lived inference sessions are blocking route teardown.

Mike L: On it. Running a graceful connection drain check:
```
ssh gateway-canary-2
ss -tnp | grep inference | wc -l
# -> 12
lsof -p <pid> | grep ESTABLISHED
```
I can force-close idle connections but want to avoid killing active customer sessions.

Santiago: Customer impact update: acme-corp incidentally used websockets for long polls; they hit 502 but later reconnected. I'll message their account rep now: @account-ops please note partial disruption 14:18-14:30 UTC, follow-up pending.

Emma H: Plan proposal:
1) Mark canary-A as quarantined in the console (prevent new deployments).
2) Manually reduce weight to 0 via traffic-router CLI.
3) If shards don't drain after 3m, force-close idle connections on gateway shards.
4) Rollback canary by traffic-router pin back to stable model variant v2026.03.14.
5) Run smoke tests and synthetic requests until metrics return to baseline.
6) Handoff to next oncall with updates and timeline.

Raj P: Executing step 2 now: `traffic-router set-weight canary-a 0 --force` -> output:
```
Updating shard 1... ok
Updating shard 2... stuck (12 active conns)
Updating shard 3... ok
```

OpsBot: shard-2 drain timeout will expire in 180s. Use `traffic-router force-evict-shard shard-2` to forcibly move connections (danger: may break ongoing sessions).

Mike L: I'll attempt graceful close of idle sessions first: `for pid in $(pgrep -f gateway-process) ; do python scripts/close-idle.py $pid --idle-secs 30 ; done`.

Avani: Meanwhile flags API is flaky; opened incident INC-flag-8821 for flags service. If we rely on flag toggles we may get partial toggles across regions.

Mike L: After close-idle run: active conns dropped to 4 (from 12). OpsBot drain retried and shard-2 updated -> success.

incident-bot: traffic-router job tr-9832 completed. canary-a weight = 0. Rollout state: quarantined.

Emma H: Great. Next step: rollback artifact to last known-good release. Raj can you trigger rollback to v2026.03.14 and pin stable? Include change in runtime config to disable the canary feature.

Raj P: Initiating rollback: `deployctl rollback redwood-inference-gateway --to v2026.03.14 --reason 'canary high 5xx'` -> job deploy-7741 created. Expected ~2m.

OpsBot: deploy-7741 progress: preflight checks passed -> starting rollout.

Santiago: Starting verification checklist (assigning self):
- [x] Canary weight = 0
- [ ] Smoke endpoint: /health (should return 200)
- [ ] Synthetic sample request /generate with standard prompt (compare token-level latency)
- [ ] Check SLOs: p50/p95/p99 and 5xx rate
- [ ] Confirm customer reconnections (acme-corp)

Mike L: Smoke test output after rollback rolled through per shard:
```
curl -sS https://gw.example/health -> 200 OK
curl -sS https://gw.example/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' -> 200, latency p50 120ms (baseline 110ms)
```

Avani: Flags service still degraded but not required now. Noting follow-ups: increase flags API horizontal autoscale, add a 2nd region replica.

Emma H: Customer comms: Santiago please coordinate an outbound note to acme-corp and finlytics with timeline and apology; include temporary mitigation steps and invite to incident review.

Santiago: Will do. Drafting now and looping in account-ops + legal. ETA 30m.

Raj P: Rollback finished and pinned. deploy-7741 -> success (ts: 2470014240). Traffic back to stable variant.

OpsBot: Post-rollback checks: 5xx < 0.5% over last 5m, latency back within 5% of baseline. Marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated at 2026-03-15T15:12:25Z (ts: 2470015945) - switching to postmortem mode. Pager cleared for oncall.

Emma H: Handoff notes for next oncall:
- Root cause suspected: a model variant change in canary introduced a regression under longer-lived websocket sessions, causing increased 502s + flags API strain.
- Actions taken: drained canary, forced eviction after idle-close, rolled back to v2026.03.14, smoke tests pass.
- Follow-ups: flags autoscale (Avani), add drain-timeout metric and alert (Mike), add canary rollout gating for websocket usage (Raj), incident writeup & timeline (Emma + Santiago).

Avani: I'll own flags autoscale ticket and add runbook entry. ticket: TKT-54321

Mike L: I'll add a runbook entry for shard drain troubleshooting and a safe-evict checklist. TKT-54322

Santiago: I'll send the customer note and draft the postmortem. Expect first draft within 48h.

Emma H: Thanks all. Closing thread once postmortem doc link is posted.

:thumbsup: reactions from Raj P, Mike L, Avani
